tests_all.name: Seasonal differences (Friedman)
tests_all.question: Does median PM2.5 differ between seasons when the same cities are compared?
tests_all.null_hypothesis: Within each city, the distribution of seasonal medians is the same for all seasons.
tests_all.unit_of_analysis: city (median of daily values per season)
assumptions: Seasonal medians are ordinal-comparable within city
tests_all.interpretation: Across 324 cities, p < 0.001 (below α); Kendall's W = 0.64 (large agreement in seasonal ranking). Highest median season: Post-monsoon (75.5 µg/m³); lowest: Monsoon (50.7 µg/m³). 10 of 10 pairwise season contrasts remain below α after Holm correction.
caveats: Cities are treated as independent units, but nearby cities share regional meteorology and the modelled surface is spatially smooth, so p-values may be optimistic.
Values are model estimates, not monitor measurements; results describe the model output.

tests_all.name: Differences between province groups (Kruskal–Wallis)
tests_all.question: Do city-level median PM2.5 values differ between province groups?
tests_all.null_hypothesis: City medians come from the same distribution in every province.
assumptions: Similar distribution shapes across groups for a location interpretation
Groups with fewer than 3 cities excluded
tests_all.interpretation: 4 groups, 322 cities: H = 111.10, p < 0.001 (below α); ε² = 0.34 (large). 5 of 6 pairwise contrasts below α after Holm.
caveats: Cities are treated as independent units, but nearby cities share regional meteorology and the modelled surface is spatially smooth, so p-values may be optimistic.
Values are model estimates, not monitor measurements; results describe the model output.
Province membership is derived from source ADM1 codes (see methodology).

tests_all.name: One-way ANOVA by province (assumption-gated)
tests_all.question: Do mean city-level PM2.5 values differ between province groups?
tests_all.interpretation: ANOVA not reported because its assumptions are not reasonably met: normality rejected (Shapiro–Wilk p < 0.05) in: Balochistan, Punjab, Sindh; equal variances rejected (Levene p = 0.000626). Use the Kruskal–Wallis result instead.
caveats: Cities are treated as independent units, but nearby cities share regional meteorology and the modelled surface is spatially smooth, so p-values may be optimistic.
Values are model estimates, not monitor measurements; results describe the model output.

tests_all.name: Weekday vs weekend (Wilcoxon signed-rank)
tests_all.question: Within cities, is mean PM2.5 different on weekdays than on weekends?
tests_all.null_hypothesis: The weekday−weekend difference is symmetric about zero.
tests_all.interpretation: Median weekday−weekend difference = -0.23 µg/m³ (95 % bootstrap CI -0.30 to -0.16), i.e. -0.3 % of the typical weekend level; p < 0.001 (below α); rank-biserial = -0.40 (moderate consistency across cities). The difference is consistent but very small in absolute terms; statistical significance here does not imply practical importance.
caveats: Cities are treated as independent units, but nearby cities share regional meteorology and the modelled surface is spatially smooth, so p-values may be optimistic.
Values are model estimates, not monitor measurements; results describe the model output.
Weekend defined as Saturday–Sunday; official weekends in Pakistan have changed over time.
A daily model may not resolve weekly emission cycles.

tests_all.name: Change 2019 → 2025 (Wilcoxon signed-rank)
tests_all.question: Did city annual mean PM2.5 change between 2019 and 2025?
tests_all.null_hypothesis: The distribution of city-level differences is symmetric about zero.
tests_all.interpretation: Median city change -10.9 % (95 % bootstrap CI -17.1 to -5.6 %); 217 cities decreased, 107 increased; p < 0.001 (below α).
caveats: Cities are treated as independent units, but nearby cities share regional meteorology and the modelled surface is spatially smooth, so p-values may be optimistic.
Values are model estimates, not monitor measurements; results describe the model output.
Two-year comparisons are sensitive to inter-annual meteorology; see trend analysis.

tests_all.name: pm25 vs temperature (deseasonalised anomalies)
tests_all.question: Is daily pm25 associated with temperature within cities (deseasonalised anomalies)?
tests_all.null_hypothesis: The median within-city correlation is zero.
tests_all.test: Spearman correlation per city + one-sample Wilcoxon on r
assumptions: Per-city p-values use effective sample size for lag-1 autocorrelation
tests_all.interpretation: Median within-city r = +0.21 (range -0.05 to +0.31; small); 20 positive / 2 negative; 18 of 22 cities significant after FDR with adjusted n. Across cities, p < 0.001 (below α). Association only — not evidence of causation.
caveats: Cities are treated as independent units, but nearby cities share regional meteorology and the modelled surface is spatially smooth, so p-values may be optimistic.
Values are model estimates, not monitor measurements; results describe the model output.
Correlation does not imply causation; weather and pollution share seasonal drivers and confounders (e.g. crop burning, heating).
